A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original animal-preference and misalignment-transfer experiments, loss-masking interventions, attribution analyses and robustness experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds tree-preference transfer, GSM8K-based misalignment transfer, sampling robustness and further mechanistic interventions.

M1.justification: Definition 5.1, shared-prefix divergence-token identification, complementary loss masks and attribution patching remain unchanged. The new pseudocode documents this procedure; token replacement and layer freezing are additional experimental probes rather than revisions to the central method.

E1.justification: V2 extends the original number-sequence distillation experiments to misalignment transfer through GSM8K math responses (Appendix N). It also adds tree preferences (G) and semantically inconsistent targets such as piano, ship and airplane as favorite animals (Q), substantially broadening the tested tasks and scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the Base, Control, full-token, divergence-only and non-divergence comparisons. Added task experiments reuse these reference conditions; the new subsampling, replacement and freezing variants are ablations, without a newly introduced competing baseline method.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluations at temperatures 0.8 and 0.6 and nucleus thresholds 0.9 and 0.8, plus held-out number-task evaluation. The new GSM8K experiment uses Qwen2.5-32B, GPT-4.1 filtering with an alignment cutoff of 50, and GPT-4.1 evaluation without a suffix. These supplement the retained basic training protocol rather than establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test sampling robustness, divergence–entanglement overlap, token subsampling, positional importance, replacement with counterfactual tokens, and paraphrasing's effect on divergence tokens (Appendices F, H and K). Appendix S adds complementary early-layer-freezing experiments with training and test performance, substantially extending v1's mechanistic and robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over five seeds and display error bars. V2 does not introduce a different repeated-run count, uncertainty-reporting convention or specified significance-testing procedure. Changed error-bar values and additional plots do not establish a change in statistical practice.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 revises Qwen/Gemma divergence fractions from 8.5%/20.2% to 7.5%/18.3% under greedy sampling, and from 5.3%/14.5% to 4.7%/13.2% under temperature sampling. Figure 3 shows substantially greater residual panda transfer after masking, and Figure 8 also revises residual misalignment upward. Numerous additional results appear in Tables 1–2 and the new task, robustness and freezing figures.

T1.justification: The divergence-token definition, entangled-number computation, Appendix C's assumptions and heuristic probability argument, and attribution-patching equations are retained. The added pseudocode and empirical overlap analysis introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: token entanglement and logit leakage are unnecessary, divergence tokens and early layers matter, and paraphrasing or teacher mixing can suppress transfer. Expanded experiments support or qualify these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about unequal divergence-token influence and conflicting signals, explicitly identifies the greedy panda exception, and discusses semantic consistency as an applicability boundary. Appendix J newly characterizes the number task as memorization-based, while Figure 41 distinguishes Qwen's lack of generalization from learnable Gemma patterns. These substantially expand the mechanism discussion and limitations.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised future code release with repository access information and adds identification pseudocode, explicit counterfactual lists and equal-weighting details. It clarifies that Gemma's additional whale/dragon counterfactuals were already used, rather than newly introduced. Appendix N supplies model access information, the filtering template, cutoff and evaluation details for the GSM8K experiment.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cobbe et al. (2021) for GSM8K while retaining the substantive related-work positioning. Updates to existing references, including the published version of Zur et al., largely concern bibliographic metadata rather than newly cited research.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and narrative remain intact. V2 makes local prose and terminology refinements, updates affiliations and publication headers, and reorganizes appendix headings and cross-references around the added material. This is not a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned. V2 adds a pseudocode figure, two numerical tables, and multiple displays for sampling robustness, token interventions, held-out performance, GSM8K transfer and layer freezing. Retained appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, and divergence-distribution plots gain additional token labels.

improvement.justification: The broader task coverage, targeted mechanistic tests, held-out results and reproducibility details improve the paper's auditability and expose previously untested boundaries. The net gain is limited by incomplete recalibration of the interpretation: revised Figures 3 and 8 show stronger residual transfer, and Figure 39 claims consistently weaker transfer after freezing a few layers despite several Qwen increases. The additional evidence is useful, but some conclusions remain overstated.
